text:
anya: FYI a customer on Win+Chrome behind corp proxy hit sampleapp SSE crash. stack shows JSON.parse on garbled payload.
devon: any capture or repro?
anya: minimal server dump: 
```
data: {"id":3,"text":"Hi "}

data: {"id":3,"text":"\xF0\x9F\x98"}

data: {"id":3,"text":"\x8A"}
```
proxy split an emoji across two chunks and also emitted an empty event between fragments. browser client decodes per-chunk and throws on incomplete utf8. node sdk buffered so it never hit crash.
lee: classic parity gap. sampleapp uses fetch+reader to support auth refresh. current parser: decode chunk -> split on "\n\n" -> JSON.parse each. too naive.
devon: quick wins: 1) use TextDecoder.decode(bytes, {stream:true}) + keep leftover bytes, 2) ignore empty events (blank lines), 3) reset parser buffer when server emits comment markers like ":resume" on reauth.
anya: another bug: when auth refresh reconnects the client, some implementations append leftover bytes from previous conn into new stream without resetting, causing concatenated objects like `..."lo"}{"id":4...` that break parse. comment-reset would prevent that.
lee: i'll draft a small sse-parser util with API feed(bytes) and reset(). It will: streaming-decode, maintain Uint8Array leftover, accumulate utf8-safe text, split events on double newline but also use a small brace-balance heuristic to accept JSON that spans boundaries.
devon: add tests: proxy-mock that injects random CRLFs, splits utf8 codepoints, and inserts ":resume <token>" comments. run in CI matrix (win/chrome + node).
ci-bot: queued test job sampleapp/streaming-resilience-proxy.
devx-bot: issue RDW-3001 created: "sse parser: make sampleapp and browser-sdk resilient to proxy CRLFs, utf8 splits, and auth-reconnects" assigned to lee + devon.
anya: customer given temp workaround (disable proxy compression). please keep them updated.
devon: will open PR with parser util + unit+e2e + README blurb. plan to land small change to reduce risk. :thumbsup:
